title: Only past sins of which one seriously repents are actually remitted—not future uncommitted sins
source_text: XXI. Igitur nulli debent dici peccata remissa, priusquam in Christum crediderit, & peccatorum suorum poenitentiam egerit. Quum vero aliquis credit & convertitur, tum demum ei remissio peccatorum actu conceditur; Sed peccatorum quae hactenus ab ipso commissa sunt, & quorum illum serio poenitet, non vero, ut nonnulli videntur, etiam futurorum. Omnino enim est contra rationem, ut dicamus peccata quae nondum commissa sunt actu esse remissa. Etenim tum demum peccatum remittitur, quum solvitur reatus, quo aliquis constrictus ob peccatum tenetur. Ac proinde peccatum remitti non potest, ubi nullus est ortus ex peccato reatus. Sed nemo reus est ob peccatum futurum, & nondum admissum. Quandoquidem reatus est relatio quaedam ex posito peccato resultans, & quae ad positionem peccati consequitur. Et certe si aliquis esset ob futurum peccatum reus, homo in statu innocentiae ante peccatum jam reus fuisset, & opus habuisset remissione peccatorum. Sed implicat contradictionem, aliquem simul reum & innocentem esse, & cum prorsus peccato careat, illum tamen remissione peccatorum egere. Nec ullus Theologus de Adamo ante lapsum istud dicere sustineat, nempe illum in eo statu jam tum indiguisse ut Deus illi peccata remitteret.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore to no one ought sins to be said remitted before he has believed in Christ and done repentance for his sins. But when someone believes and is converted, then at last remission of sins is actually granted to him—but of the sins which have thus far been committed by him and of which he seriously repents, not also, as some seem to hold, of future ones. For it is altogether against reason that we should say sins which have not yet been committed are actually remitted. For a sin is remitted only then when the guilt is loosed by which someone is bound on account of sin. And therefore a sin cannot be remitted where no guilt has arisen from sin. But no one is guilty on account of a future sin not yet admitted. Since guilt is a certain relation resulting from sin posited, and which follows upon the positing of sin. And certainly if someone were guilty on account of a future sin, a man in the state of innocence before sin would already have been guilty and would have needed remission of sins. But it implies a contradiction that someone be at once guilty and innocent, and that, though he wholly lacks sin, he nevertheless need remission of sins. Nor would any theologian dare say that of Adam before the fall—namely that in that state he already needed God to remit sins to him.
pass_b_english: Actual remission at faith/repentance covers past sins seriously repented—not futures not yet done.
No guilt-relation without posited sin; pre-fall Adam needing pardon is a contradiction.

choices.why: Denied as already actually remitted at conversion.
